```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r}
a <- 17
b <- 5
a + b
a - b
a * b
a / b

a %% b
a %/% b

2^10
```
Q1. When we divide 17 by 5, we get 3.4 as the exact result. The integer division  17 %/% 5  gives 3, which is the whole-number part, and  17 %% 5  gives 2, the remainder left over. Together they show that 17 equals 5 multiplied by 3 plus 2, and the decimal part 0.4 comes from dividing the remainder 2 by 5.
Q2. I predicted  10 %% 3  would be 1 and  10 %/% 3  would be 3, because 10 divided by 3 gives 3 whole times with 1 left over. I was correct because 3 × 3 = 9, so the remainder is indeed 1. If I had been wrong, it would have meant I mixed up which operator finds the remainder and which finds the whole number.
